tagline: Sync engineering metrics and issue data to Airtable dashboards
metaDescription: Mirror Linear issues and cycle metrics to Airtable bases and build bug triage views. GAIA keeps the data current. See the setup steps.
intro:
Linear is purpose-built for engineering teams. Airtable is purpose-built for structured data that non-technical stakeholders can query, filter, and build views on. The two serve different audiences, but the data that lives in Linear — issue counts, cycle velocity, lead times, label breakdowns — is exactly what operations, finance, and product leadership want to analyze in Airtable.

GAIA syncs this data automatically so dashboards stay current without anyone manually exporting CSVs. Engineering metrics land in bases where stakeholders can build the views, formulas, and reports they need without accessing the issue tracker. When an issue is created, updated, or completed, the matching row reflects the change in real time.

This integration is particularly useful for ops teams that track engineering KPIs alongside other business metrics in a shared base, and for companies that use their bases as the source of truth for cross-functional reporting.

useCases.title: Mirror Linear issues to an Airtable issues base
useCases.description: GAIA creates a row in Airtable for each issue in your configured scope, keeping fields like status, assignee, priority, label, and cycle synchronized so stakeholders can query, filter, and group issues without Linear access.

useCases.title: Sync cycle metrics to an engineering KPIs base
useCases.description: At the end of each cycle, GAIA appends a new record to the engineering KPIs base with velocity, completion rate, carry-over percentage, and average cycle time so leadership can track engineering health over time.

useCases.title: Build bug triage views in Airtable
useCases.description: GAIA syncs all issues labeled bug to a dedicated base where the support team can add triage notes, customer impact ratings, and reproduction steps that live alongside the engineering issue data without cluttering the issue tracker.

useCases.title: Track feature delivery commitments
useCases.description: GAIA syncs issues linked to committed features to a tracking base. Stakeholders see target cycle, current status, and actual delivery date in a format they can embed in executive reports.

useCases.title: Aggregate team capacity data for resource planning
useCases.description: GAIA writes assigned issue counts, story points, and cycle allocations per engineer to a resource planning base so ops and engineering management can model capacity without manual data collection.

howItWorks.step: Connect Linear and Airtable to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Linear workspace and Airtable account. Select or create the base and tables that should receive the data.

howItWorks.step: Map issue fields to table columns
howItWorks.description: Define which issue properties map to which table columns. GAIA supports all standard fields as well as custom fields and will create columns for any that do not already exist.

howItWorks.step: The tables stay current as issues change
howItWorks.description: GAIA watches for issue changes and propagates them to the base in near real time. Stakeholders always see current data in their views without anyone running exports.

faqs.question: Does GAIA sync historical Linear issues or only new activity?
faqs.answer: On initial setup, GAIA performs a historical backfill of all existing issues within your configured scope. Going forward, new issues and updates sync in near real time.

faqs.question: Can Airtable team members update rows and have those changes reflected back in the issue tracker?
faqs.answer: Bidirectional sync is supported for a limited set of fields — primarily status and assignee. For most teams, the issue tracker is treated as the authoritative source and the base is read-optimized, but you can enable write-back for specific columns during setup.

faqs.question: How does GAIA handle deleted issues?
faqs.answer: When an issue is deleted, GAIA marks the corresponding row as archived rather than deleting it, so your historical reporting data is preserved. You can configure hard deletion if your data retention policy requires it.
